record.reviewer: Codex assistant in this chat, reviewing final responses and helper artifacts against evals/README.md

results.note: App-owned phargus:start/phargus:collect recipes use copied .phargus/tools; initial capture had 6 windows/8 spans and restart had 6 windows/10 spans. Raw restart summary showed 7 samples/10 spans. Kept SSE loss unknown and sourceCommitVerified false; verified closed app/dashboard connections after cleanup.

Rerun preserved the actual helper JSON in tool-result.json. Correctly contrasted 10 versus 400 ms requests with identical loop/GC/backpressure signals; kept dependency waiting and synchronous work as hypotheses and proposed controlled stream-drain experiments plus per-operation timing.
Comparison is inconclusive: 100 vs 60 declared requests and 3000 ms declared duration versus 6000 ms recorded; zero measurement deltas are not evidence of improvement under mismatched conditions.

RSS rose 20 to 70 MiB, external 2 to 52 MiB and arrayBuffers 1 to 51 MiB with heap flat at 1/4 MiB. Identified external/ArrayBuffer pressure without proving a leak or attributing the hotspot as a cause; proposed repeated workload/drain cycles and post-cycle baselines.

Executable alert uses eventLoop.max > 50,000,000 ns for 2 windows. The exact 50 ms window is excluded; incident fires at 3000 ms and resolves at 4000 ms, while normal replay has no alerts. Activation includes a delivery sink.

An empty recording is insufficient evidence, with loss unknown and no root-cause or health claim. Proposed raw captures during slow and normal periods with request spans and matched measurement conditions.

Real 500 ms dashboard capture produced 6 historical windows and no live updates/spans. Reported SSE loss unknown and backpressure call sites/external/arrayBuffers memory unavailable; proposed raw workload captures instead of attributing a request cause.
Reported event-loop maximum 100 ms and maximum sample p99 90 ms, explicitly refusing to reconstruct a global percentile from sample aggregates.

App-owned start:phargus/phargus:collect/verify.sh recipes use copied .phargus/tools, @pharn-dev/phargus/agent and PHARGUS_OUTPUT. Initial and restart SSE each contained 8 windows/10 spans. Kept SSE loss unknown; trap stopped processes and dashboard port was closed.

Reported 10 ms median/400 ms request tail, 100 ms event-loop maximum, 2 ms GC and 3 ms backpressure maxima with flat memory. Kept synchronous work and dependency waiting as hypotheses, stated no CPU stacks/outgoing spans, and proposed raw time alignment plus handler timing. Minor: it did not note that fast/slow periods share identical runtime signals.

Kept the comparison inconclusive because requests differ (100 versus 60) and recorded duration/coverage is 6000 ms versus 3000 ms declared; identical latency/other deltas do not establish a controlled improvement.

Identified the same external/ArrayBuffer growth with flat JS heap; kept leak and hotspot causation unproven and proposed controlled cycles. Minor: future heap-diff wording suggests finding owners, beyond this helper's object-count/self-size output and lack of retaining paths.

Used strict > 50,000,000 ns for 2 windows; equality did not breach. Incident fired at 3000 ms/resolved at 4000 ms and normal replay stayed empty. Gave collector/helper activation plus file-sink delivery verification.
Empty input produced no observations of request/runtime health; loss stays unknown. Explicitly refused a cause and requested nonempty slow/normal captures with workload conditions.

500 ms SSE capture had 6 historical windows and no live updates/spans. Kept loss unknown and hotspots/external/arrayBuffers unavailable. Minor: follow-up wording about enabling memory fields and heap diffs overstates the contract; raw Phargus samples are the appropriate source for those memory categories.
Reported 100 ms event-loop maximum and 90 ms maximum sample p99; explicitly said a global recording p99 cannot be reconstructed from those aggregates.
